subject: confidence intervals on parameters differ between STAN and JAGS?

messages.author: 7dd668eb41c5bfd9
messages.subject: confidence intervals on parameters differ between STAN and JAGS?
parts:
Super quick question:

I'm playing with the radon data (the group-level predictor example). I fit the STAN model using the example code posted online. Then, I redid the model to be more similar to the BUGS code, where the intercepts are a function of county-level uranium (as an aside, is STAN like lmer in that it figures out when a predictor is on the group level? In the example code online, the county-level uranium looks like it's at the individual level but STAN seems to figure out that it's at the county level). The STAN output matches lmer almost exactly, and both STAN variants give nearly identical parameter estimates (0.7 +/- 0.1) and confidence intervals (0.1 - 0.9) for the group-level coefficient (g1), although estimates of the county-level intercepts differ between models (but they're being modeled differently, so I expect that).

Then I ran the model in JAGS using the code from ARM (Chapter 12, pg. 361).

However, the JAGS model estimates the group-level coefficient g1 less precisely (although g0 seems to be similar), with a mean of 0.65 +/- 0.22 and a confidence interval of 0.21 - 1.1. I looked through the manual and the previous posts to see if this had come up, but I couldn't find anything. I did notice that JAGS and STAN estimate the county-level intercepts similarly (when running comparable models, albeit JAGS is again more imprecise), just the county-level regression coefficient differs.

My super quick question is: is it normal or to be expected that STAN gives more precise than JAGS/BUGS due to its different sampling algorithm? I was pretty surprised that JAGS was so imprecise for that parameter.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] confidence intervals on parameters differ between STAN and JAGS?
parts:
What the relative effective sample sizes?  Remember that the quantiles are just estimators, and they can
be pretty noise for low ESS.  Stan shouldn’t be giving a different posterior, but it’s greater efficiency may
lead to more accurate estimates of the quantiles that deviate from the JAGS estimates.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] confidence intervals on parameters differ between STAN and JAGS?
parts:
> On Jan 28, 2014, at 4:47 PM, Nathan Lemoine <lemoine...@gmail.com <mailto:lemoine...@gmail.com>> wrote:

>> ... as an aside, is STAN like lmer in that it figures out when a predictor is on the group level? In

>> the example code online, the county-level uranium looks like it's at the individual level but STAN seems to figure out
>> that it's at the county level

Are you talking about one of the ARM examples? If so, which one?
It looks like there are a lot of Radon examples.

To answer your question, Stan only does what's written in the
model --- it doesn't try to get clever and figure out user intent.

I would guess that lmer also only does what's in the model expression,
but I'm not sure about that.

Also, lmer is only approximating the posterior confidence intervals using
curvature at the solution, whereas Stan's estimating the posterior intervals
using sampling. Quantiles (boundaries of intervals) require more effective samples to
estimate than means or medians, because, for example, the 5% quantile is only based on
the smallest 5% of the samples.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] confidence intervals on parameters differ between STAN and JAGS?
parts:
Oh --- just saw that your original post had the model.
Nothing in their is grouped at the ocunty level other
than the varying intercept b. If u is the Uranium
predictor, then it varies by county as well, but the
coefficient beta[2] doesn't --- it's shared across all
of the u[i].

- bob

P.S. Here's the model:

data {
int<lower=0> N;
int<lower=1,upper=85> county[N];
vector[N] u;
vector[N] x;
vector[N] y;
}
parameters {
vector[85] b;
vector[2] beta;
real mu_b;
real mu_beta;
real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma;
real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_b;
real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_beta;
}
transformed parameters {
vector[N] y_hat;

for (i in 1:N)
y_hat[i] <- b[county[i]] + x[i] * beta[1] + u[i] * beta[2];
}
model {
mu_b ~ normal(0, 1);
b ~ normal(mu_b, sigma_b);

mu_beta ~ normal(0, 1);
beta ~ normal(100 * mu_beta, sigma_beta);

y ~ normal(y_hat, sigma);
}

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] confidence intervals on parameters differ between STAN and JAGS?
parts:
I guess what I meant is that lmer/lme seems to "figure out" that u is a county-level predictor and treats the denominator degrees of freedom accordingly, but I guess this is more related to hypothesis testing than parameter estimates. It just seemed a little odd to me to use u as the full vector where u[i,j] are identical within a county [j], rather than the "traditional" approach of making the intercept a[j] a function of u[j]. I'm not used to thinking about it that way. This stems more from an incomplete understanding of the way the model is structured on my part. I always thought it was necessary to remove the duplicate u[i]'s (within a county), otherwise the parameter might be estimated too precisely (i.e. assuming there are more data points than actually are present).

I guess, pedagogically, it's easier for me to think about the model (using the full u vector) as (a[county[i]] + b2*u[i] ) + b1*x[i], which more clearly shows the intercept varying at the group level (and the effect of u on that intercept).
